classification.difficultyReason: Links substitution in supplied tables to coordinate plots and two separate reciprocal branches, recognising undefined values at zero and the signed approach to zero at each infinity.

content.prompt: Plot $y=\frac{2}{x}$ and $y=\frac{3}{x}$ on the same axis.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1, shared graph on the right
spec.description: Portrait Cartesian grid with unit grid spacing, x from −4 to 4 and y from −10 to 10. Every nonzero integer is labelled; both axes have arrowheads at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Common coordinate frame for y=2/x and y=3/x.
spec.answerVisibility: Blank axes and grid remain visible in Questions; completed curves belong to the answer graph.

inlines.text: Substitute each nonzero x-value into the equation. Division by zero is undefined, so there is no point at
. The behaviour explanations and graph follow below.

answer.worked: As positive $x$ increases, $\frac2x$ remains positive and approaches zero: $y\to0^+$.
As negative $x$ decreases, $\frac2x$ remains negative and approaches zero: $y\to0^-$.

answer.worked: As positive $x$ increases, $\frac3x$ remains positive and approaches zero: $y\to0^+$.
As negative $x$ decreases, $\frac3x$ remains negative and approaches zero: $y\to0^-$.

answer.short: Both graphs have branches in quadrants I and III and asymptotes $x=0$ and $y=0$. See graph.
answer.worked: Plot the coordinate pairs from each completed table. Join each set with two smooth branches, keeping the branches separate across $x=0$. Both curves approach the coordinate axes. For the same nonzero $x$, $y=\frac3x$ lies farther from the $x$-axis than $y=\frac2x$.
